title: "Russian Bayonet, Chinese Yuan": Functional Asymmetry of Great Powers in Central Asia (1992–2022)
content: This paper introduces the analytical formula "Russian Bayonet, Chinese Yuan" — a conceptual construct describing the stable functional asymmetry between Russia and China in Central Asia over the period 1992–2022. By functional asymmetry the paper means a historically consolidated, structurally reproduced, but never treaty-codified division of dominant roles: Russia as the primary provider of security guarantees and political stability; China as the dominant source of infrastructural financing and economic expansion through the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). The paper acknowledges that this asymmetry was not absolute: China gradually increased its security presence while Russian economic influence through migration channels remained substantial. The paper is conceptual in character; its aim is to introduce the formula into academic circulation, propose operationalizable proxy indicators for subsequent empirical verification, and map the stress-testing logic using counterfactual cases. The theoretical basis is the author's concept of Infrastructure Projection of Geopolitics (IPG; Rakhimov, 2026). The paper argues that the structural fracture of 2022 initiated a process of reconfiguration of this arrangement — without instantly destroying it.
